How to read this reference

Namespace and names

The public graph and RHI APIs share the flat arda namespace. Qualified names identify the owning namespace or class; short names can match overloads, template specializations, or members on several types.

Graph identity and generations

Node and resource handles carry graph identity, an index, and a generation. Removing an entry invalidates its handle; a replacement cannot silently inherit that identity. Handles from another graph are rejected. Physical RHI references are resolved through the execution context for declared node accesses.

Edit and execute phases

Make graph changes through FArdaGraphEdit operations and check the commit status. Compile() queues asynchronous Rendering work to select a cached persistent revision or invoke ArdaInductor. You may enqueue execution immediately: its RHI job waits in reserve for compilation and checks the captured compile result before hardware work begins. Inspect returned receipt results for failure. Ordinary execution favors ready independent graphs; ordered execution additionally follows earlier graph hardware jobs. Pending jobs keep authoring closed, and successful compilation stages the construction until a submission or execution attempt. The next ordinary edit starts an empty construction, and matching frame constructions reuse the selected revision and prepared runtime. The first submission materializes native resources, pipelines and bindings.

Status and lookup contracts

Registration, compilation, and execution report failures through their documented status/result types. Lookups can return an empty result for a missing or stale identity. A failed edit must be corrected before execution; do not treat a failed compilation as a usable schedule.

Resources and ownership

The graph owns node records and frozen typed parameters. Graph-created resources receive storage from the memory plan; imported resources retain their RHI references. Resource outputs root observable work, and persistent resources retain contents between executions. Imported textures enter and leave in the initialized, uniform state captured during first-submission materialization. The caller must preserve that state between executions.

Submission and GPU completion

Submit() records and submits on the caller and returns a frame ticket while GPU work can still be pending. Poll with Graph.IsComplete(Ticket). Call Graph.Wait(Ticket) to retire the frame and publish readbacks. Execute() performs both steps. Frame slots retain submitted resources through completion.

Recording and resource declarations

FArdaDependencyExecutionContext supplies the command list, declared physical resources, and automatically assigned pipelines. A node must declare every graph resource it accesses. Independently retained RHI references cannot supply missing dependency or lifetime information to ArdaInductor.

Typed node definitions

Register a parameter type with its resource description, canonical identity, and execution callbacks through the singleton node registry. Record immutable parameters through a callable node object: const FMyNode Node{}; Node(Edit, Parameters), or pass positional schema fields with Node(Edit, Arg1, Arg2, ...). The equivalent unnamed call is FMyNode{}(Edit, ...). Static FMyNode::Invoke and registry-driven Edit.Invoke share the same operation path. Canonical keys must include every value that changes the node's behavior or dependencies. CUDA definitions can prepare compiled kernels or external library calls; ArdaInductor coalesces compatible adjacent CUDA nodes into one execution sequence.

arda::FArdaDependencyGraph
class FArdaDependencyGraph final

Persistent dependency graph, edited transactionally and executed repeatedly across frames. Single-producer regions resolve independently of attachment order. Regions with multiple producers order reads and writes by original node attachment, preserving the preceding value until its readers finish. Disjoint regions remain independent. Public authoring uses resource operations and Node::Invoke. FArdaGraphEdit::Commit queues an ordered construction edit. Compile runs on the calling thread, selecting a cached revision or invoking ArdaInductor. Submit records and submits one frame on the calling thread and returns its GPU ticket. Execute also waits for frame completion. The next ordinary edit starts empty. Failed compilation retains queued edits for correction or DiscardPendingEdits. Separate threads may record and commit independent edit scopes concurrently. Explicit shared-resource revisions order those edits before hazard analysis; otherwise commit order defines attachment order. Each scope sees the construction committed before it opened. Graph inspection on an editing thread reads its private snapshot. A successful Compile locks authoring until a Submit/Execute attempt; later reference-returning inspection remains valid after that attempt returns.

Ownership
Owning handles retain their object; pointer and reference parameters are borrowed unless stated otherwise.
Errors
Failures and unsupported operations use the declared FArdaRHIStatus or TArdaRHIResult contract.
Threading
Calls follow the synchronization rules of the owning provider device or command list.

arda::FArdaGraphEdit
class FArdaGraphEdit final

Begins a private graph edit and records operations in call order. The first authoring failure is retained; later operations do nothing and Commit returns that failure. Cancel and start a new scope to recover. Destruction cancels an uncommitted transaction, preserving the previous executable graph. Never manually end/reopen its transaction while a scope is active. Commit only queues declarations; call Graph.Compile after closing all edits before execution. Graph must outlive this scope. Distinct threads may own independent scopes concurrently; each scope itself stays in its opening thread through closure. Recording is private; only publication is serialized. A scope sees prior committed edits, never another scope's uncommitted declarations. Concurrent explicit operation-name, unversioned import or option collisions fail Commit atomically. Versioned imports share one logical identity for the same physical storage; SetResourceRevision orders their edits before compilation.

Ownership
Owning handles retain their object; pointer and reference parameters are borrowed unless stated otherwise.
Errors
Failures and unsupported operations use the declared FArdaRHIStatus or TArdaRHIResult contract.

Calls follow the synchronization rules of the owning provider device or command list.

arda::TArdaExecutionNode
template <class Derived, class Parameters, EArdaDependencyNodeKind Kind = EArdaDependencyNodeKind::Compute> class TArdaExecutionNode : public FArdaDependencyNodeBase

Master CRTP node contract, deriving from FArdaDependencyNodeBase without virtual dispatch. Derived supplies static GetMetadata() -> FArdaDependencyNodeMetadata, GetCanonicalKey(const FArdaParameters&) -> eastl::string and Describe(const FArdaParameters&, const FArdaState&) -> FArdaDependencyNodeDesc. Macro-authored parameter structs provide default identity and resource descriptions; Describe may add pipeline contributions or parameter-dependent effects to those declarations. Native nodes implement Record(Context&, const FArdaParameters&, const FArdaState&, FArdaInstanceState&) returning FArdaRHIStatus. CUDA nodes instead implement PrepareCuda with the same arguments plus FArdaCudaSequence& and append operations without submitting. Synchronization may omit execution. GetMetadata must be stable; canonical keys cover every behavior-affecting parameter and full resource identity without structure padding. Describe must declare all resource accesses and pipeline needs. Override FArdaState/Prepare for immutable device setup and FArdaInstanceState/CreateInstance for private mutable operation state. The graph prepares declared shader bindings and tables. Opaque state types may be declared in a node header and defined in its .cpp. Preparation is fixed by node type/device; parameter-dependent setup belongs in CreateInstance and its memory requirements in Describe. Do not submit GPU work in preparation hooks.

Ownership
The base retains immutable parameter snapshots, prepared state and per-instance state. Nested pointees are not deep-copied; keep semantic inputs immutable and synchronize dynamic inputs. Weak device-state cache entries do not extend state or device lifetime after the last instance releases them.
Errors
Incomplete node contracts fail at registration/attachment compilation. Preparation failures propagate without insertion; successful null state results return InvalidState. Name collisions are InvalidArgument.
Threading
Registration and device preparation are serialized per class. Shared state is immutable. Distinct threads may record private graph edit scopes concurrently; publication is atomic at Commit. Each edit belongs to one thread; submission and general graph inspection require external synchronization. Private operation state may mutate during recording, following declared resource effects and frame lifetimes.
Source

arda::TArdaNodeArray
template <class Value> class TArdaNodeArray final

An owning array of node arguments or invocation results. Passing this wrapper at any positional parameter slot invokes one logical operation per element. All array arguments must have equal lengths; scalar arguments are copied to every lane. This is zip/broadcast semantics, not a Cartesian product. Empty arrays produce no operations. Ordinary vectors and shader parameter arrays remain single parameter values unless explicitly wrapped. Invocation freezes each parameter value before returning; nested pointees retain normal shared ownership semantics. The compiler resolves dependencies/pipelines and batches the logical lanes.

Ownership
Owning handles retain their object; pointer and reference parameters are borrowed unless stated otherwise.
Errors

Compute/native operations implement Record; CUDA implements PrepareCuda and may supply RecordComputeAlternative for devices without CUDA. All nodes inherit CheckRequiredFeatures. Graphics stages implement ConfigureGraphics and return typed state. Ray providers return typed shader references, and a ray-generation terminal implements Record to dispatch its assembled pipeline and shader table.

arda::EArdaGraphicsInstancing
enum class EArdaGraphicsInstancing : uint8_t

Explicit semantic permission for automatic instancing of a graphics stage. ContiguousInstances promises ConfigureGraphics only fills Work, without recording commands, changing external or instance state, or relying on a draw boundary. Shader behavior must be invariant when adjacent instance ranges become one draw, including instance-ID addressing. D3D SV_InstanceID is relative to each draw; it alone cannot index a globally based instance table. Prefer per-instance vertex inputs or another explicitly base-aware, merge-invariant shader contract. Every stage in a traditional draw must opt in. Geometry, bindings and ranges are still checked.

arda::AllocateInitializedBuffer
FArdaGraphBuffer AllocateInitializedBuffer(FArdaGraphEdit& Edit, const FArdaRHIBufferDesc& Description, eastl::vector<uint8_t> Bytes, eastl::string Name = {})

Declares a persistent GPU buffer initialized from an owned, nonempty byte prefix. Attachment and logical compilation perform no GPU work. Cold physical preparation uploads and waits for this data once per new allocation, before any graph execution. Subsequent frames and compatible revisions preserve the allocation and its contents without reuploading. Bytes after the prefix remain uninitialized; a producer must write them before reading.

arda::ARDA_DECLARE_GRAPH_NODE
#define ARDA_DECLARE_GRAPH_NODE(NodeClass, InvocationName)

Declare a named, immutable callable immediately after its node class at namespace scope. Put the matching ARDA_DEFINE_GRAPH_NODE in exactly one source file in the same namespace. The externally linked object has one identity across translation units; names must be unique within their namespace. Declaration registers the type without preparing any device state.

NodeClass
Complete class derived from TArdaNodeDefinition.
InvocationName
Public C++ operation name, independent of the class and registry names.
Ownership
Owning handles retain their object; pointer and reference parameters are borrowed unless stated otherwise.

arda::FArdaDependencyExecutionContext::ReadbackTexture
FArdaRHIStatus ReadbackTexture(FArdaDependencyResourceHandle Resource, eastl::shared_ptr<eastl::vector<uint8_t>> Destination, const FArdaRHITextureSlice& Slice = {}) const

Records a graphics-queue texture readback with completion-safe publication. Resource must declare the selected subresource in CopySource state. Supports typed, single-sample, uncompressed color regions. Output contains tightly packed rows in increasing Y order, followed by increasing Z slices; native row padding is removed after completion. The retained destination follows ReadbackBuffer's successful-frame and failure semantics. Declare mTransientWorkspaceBytes at least GetArdaRHITextureBufferFootprint(...).mValue.mByteSize. The graph budgets and allocates this workspace per frame; its UAV state is restored after recording.

Source/ArdaInfra/ArdaDependencyGraph/Public/Graph/Node/ArdaDependencyGraph.h
arda::FArdaDependencyGraph::Compile
[[nodiscard]] FArdaRHIStatus Compile(bool bForceRecompile = false)

Compile on the calling thread and return final diagnostics. Apply the ordered queue and stage a persistent executable revision. Matching constructions reuse cached topology, compilation and runtime. Success clears the queue and locks edits until Execute/Submit is attempted. Failure preserves the queue for repair or DiscardPendingEdits. With no queued construction, re-stage the current persistent graph. Force bypasses cache lookup. Switching revisions retires the outgoing runtime's submissions; reusing that same runtime preserves frame-slot overlap. Requires closed edits and no outstanding staged execution lock. Compiler rules and callbacks run on this thread. Reentrant graph mutation is rejected.

arda::FArdaDependencyGraph::Submit
[[nodiscard]] TArdaRHIResult<FArdaDependencyFrameTicket> Submit(const FArdaGraphExecuteOptions& Options = {})

Record and submit one frame on the calling thread, returning its GPU frame ticket. Materialize the pending plan on first submission, then submit a frame. Preparation failure returns a diagnostic without publishing a frame and retains the plan for retry. Later submissions reuse the runtime, waiting only when recycling an occupied frame slot. Before hardware work begins, Compile must have succeeded with no pending construction. Attempting submission unlocks editing, including on submission failure; another submission without new edits retries the selected revision. The ticket may still have GPU work in flight; poll with IsComplete(ticket). Wait(ticket) retires the frame and publishes readbacks.

Fill fresh parameters synchronously, then record one operation. The initializer returns void or FArdaRHIStatus; failures are retained by the edit. The optional name is diagnostic and unique.

Returns
See the declared result and status contract.
Ownership
Owning handles retain their object; pointer and reference parameters are borrowed unless stated otherwise.
Errors
Failures and unsupported operations use the declared FArdaRHIStatus or TArdaRHIResult contract.
Threading
Calls follow the synchronization rules of the owning provider device or command list.
